The spirit of the Old and New Testaments is one, and their agreement is one, 605 ff. The severity of the Old Testament, or Law, has been tempered by the grace of the Gospel, 116. The testimonies of both Testaments concerning Christ wonderfully agree with one another, 31. The treasures of the Roman Church are spent by Saint Lawrence on assisting the poor, 240. What is the treasure which, according to the Apostle, 2 Corinthians XVIII [as printed], we have in earthen vessels? 593. Thomas, touching the wounds of the risen Christ, recognized in him a true body and confirmed everyone’s faith in his resurrection, 480. To God again, 181 ff. Spiritual enemies are more to be feared than bodily ones, according to Christ’s statement in Matthew X: “Do not fear those who kill the body,” etc., 294. One who has feared Christ the Savior cannot fear barbarians, ibid. The fear we owe to God, 297. Tobias’s charity in burying the dead is commended, 381. Christ’s Transfiguration on Mount Tabor: why Christ appeared with Moses and Elijah, and why there were only three witnesses among the apostles, 769. The crossing of the Red Sea by the children of Israel, marked by many wonders, 61. The straits of tribulations open the way to the fullness of joys, 624. In tribulation it is good to pray, fast, sing psalms, and show mercy, 291. Tribute must be paid to secular rulers, 377.

## U

What the anointing of the ears with blessed oil before baptism signifies, 710. The second anointing, on the nostrils, is explained, 712. Through sacred anointing in the Old Testament, priests and kings were established; this was conferred by prophets, 717. The crime of usury is condemned, 128. The nature of usury is described, 349. Through usury the creditor is remunerated by the debt, yet the debt is not extinguished, ibid.

## V

The display of vainglory is censured, 104. The vanities and follies of the world are rebuked, 42. Whatever possesses no weight or firmness of virtue is vain and empty, ibid. What does the vessel full of animals of every kind that appeared to Peter signify? 575. Through Adam’s transgression we were vessels of wrath; through Christ’s resurrection we have become citizens of the saints, 489. Hunting is condemned during Lent, 458. The unity and co-eternity of the Word with the Father are proved against the Arians chiefly from that passage of Scripture where Christ says of himself in John XII: “I and the Father are one,” 270. We must persevere in preaching the Word of God so that we may attain the salvation of souls, 551. The Word of God works in all the faithful the substance of eternal salvation, 130. It is of no benefit to shine in clothing if someone is filthy with crimes; for when the conscience is dark, the whole body is darkened, 18. Christ’s garments, divided by the soldiers into four parts after his crucifixion, signify the prophecies that foretold the Lord, which heretics tear apart and divide in order to construct their own doctrines, 139. His seamless garment, woven from above, signifies his heavenly wisdom, ibid. What is to be understood by the garments with which the apostles spread the road for the Lord as he entered Jerusalem? 123. The way that leads to Christ is his faith and teaching, 123. The Magi come by one way to the Lord’s manger and return by another; the mystery is explained, 54, 81. Who are those who do not prepare the way for the coming Lord? How is the way to be prepared, and by what holy works is he to be met? 209, 543. How necessary victory over oneself is, 119. How “to do violence to Christ” is to be understood, 395. What is the vineyard of the Lord of hosts? 597. Mary’s virginity in giving birth, before giving birth, and after giving birth is asserted, 25. [A lacuna in the supplied text.] For virginity alone could worthily give birth to Christ, 509. If we do anything excellent by virtue, it is not to be attributed to us but to God, 309, 571. We must not trust in our own strength if we wish to be victorious over worldly dangers, 636. The beatific vision of God, to be attained by human beings, was the end and goal of Christ’s entire dispensation in the world, 520. Its essence consists in seeing God, ibid. What is the life of a Christian according to the Gospel? 265. Every wise person understands that this human life was not given for rest but for labor—that is, so that one may labor here and rest thereafter, 293. In this life, with pain and labor, let us do what is good with God’s help, so that in the future age we may receive the fruit of good things with joy and exultation, 584. We ought to regard the whole time of our life as a kind of training ground for virtues and strive with our whole mind toward the heavenly prize, 441. The one who knows how to pray rightly knows how to live rightly, 353. Vitalianus and Maianus, noble men who contributed all their possessions, though modest, to the building up of the Church, are praised, 686.

## X

Xistus [Sixtus], the Roman pontiff, foretells to his deacon Lawrence that he will soon follow him to martyrdom, 239.

## Z

Zechariah, serving as priest in the temple in the course of Abijah, received a prophecy from an angel that he would become the father of John, 559. Because he did not believe the angelic oracle, he lost the use of speech, 207. At John’s birth the bonds of his tongue were loosed, so that by this miracle the child given from heaven might be revealed and what was to be expected from him might be made known, 546. Zacchaeus is praised because, having used his riches well, he reached the heavenly kingdom through them, 654 ff. Apostolic zeal for the conversion and salvation of souls is commended, 252.

[Col. 0979]

# INDEX OF MEMORABLE MATTERS CONTAINED IN THE APPENDIX

## A

Abraham, Melchizedek, and Jacob offered tithes to God from all their possessions, 85. God revealed that the restoration of transgressing Adam, condemned together with his offspring, would be fulfilled at the end of time, 130. After his sin Adam recognized that he was naked, 145. Bodily illnesses are benefits from God. For it is better to be rebuked and chastised by the Lord and healed beneath his scourge than to be removed from his medicine as incurable, 113. The prophet Haggai was an assistant to Zechariah in the restoration of the temple at Jerusalem, 96. The condition of the worldly contest is that it makes victorious the person who overcomes his opponent by fighting bravely; in spiritual combat, however, the person who pours out his life for the truth is crowned, 55. The love of God endures all things and overcomes all things, 112. Angels announcing the newborn Lord with songs invite us to worship him, 26. The soul lives by faith, the body by the soul, 55. Whoever loses his soul for Christ will save it forever; but whoever gives it for the world will lose it, 138. The savage cruelty of King Antiochus toward the noblest Maccabean brothers is noted, 73. Before the Holy Spirit descended upon them, the apostles were timid and imperfect, 35. Noah’s ark, in which eight souls were saved, is compared with the Church, 89. Archelaus, one of Herod’s sons, succeeded him in the kingdom of Judea, 28. He died in exile at Vienne in Gaul, ibid. The heresy of Arius is refuted, 96. The perfidy and cunning of the Arians were exposed and confounded by Saint Eusebius of Vercelli, 68. What disturbances the Arians caused in Italy and throughout the world, ibid. The three qualities of the reed, 102. When the author of things has been discovered, we shall also discover the causes of things, 147. While Caesar Augustus was reigning, Judea became tributary to the Roman Empire, 99. Auxentius the Arian, bishop of Milan, was succeeded by Saint Ambrose, 146.

## B

What happiness and fullness of joy will receive the souls of the righteous in heavenly blessedness, 66. The pool of Bethsaida, whose water healed those who washed in it from their illnesses, 123. The certain promise of future good things ought to inflame us to undergo death courageously, 134.

## C

Christian charity must not be extended only to friends, 20. It should be devoted to the salvation of neighbors, 140. Nothing ought to separate us from the charity of Christ, 75. Christ’s and the Holy Spirit’s unfailing protection of the Church is promised, 35. The promise of an eternal kingdom, perpetual worship of the temple, and praise was made to Christ, not to Solomon, 21. We must confess Christ as true God and true human being, 94. The same Lord demonstrated that he both could and wished to save the human race, 119. Christ alone, the Son of God, assumed flesh in such a way, together with a rational and perfect human soul, and assumed the form of a body and the reality of this body, becoming human, 31. He was thought to be Joseph’s son, 130. He endured death and was committed to burial; but because he truly rose again, our faith is firm, 32. Risen from the dead with a new splendor of his divinity, he awakens us to joy, 89. In his resurrection the Synagogue comes to an end and the Church is born, 89. He who had raised other dead persons raised himself by his own power into the light, 129. His tomb is glorious, 21. Christ was filled with all the gifts of the Holy Spirit, 22. He deigns to dwell by faith in the hearts of his children, 55. Why did he wish to pay tribute to Caesar? 99. He created a coin in the mouth of a fish, with which Peter paid the tax for Christ and for himself, 100. Cleombrotus of Ambracia threw himself from a very high wall because he believed that everything concerning the human being ended with death, 134. The conception of John the Baptist was wondrous, but Christ’s was more wondrous. The former was born from a mother suffering from old age and barrenness; the latter was begotten from a virgin, 43 ff. Those regarded as contemptible in this life will appear in another clothed in glory and majesty, 137. How much purity must be brought to the spiritual banquet, 61. The person who entered the banquet without a wedding garment was handed over to the torturers, ibid. The body of a man thrown into Elisha’s tomb came scarcely into contact with his bones before it revived, 139. Desire is the root of all evils, 88.

## D

Tithes and firstfruits must be paid to God, 85 ff. Everything has been given to us by God; therefore everything must be returned to him, ibid. Earthly things are exchanged for eternal goods, 86. How the dedications of churches are to be celebrated, 61. Many miracles performed at them are recorded, 82 ff. At the first dedication of Solomon’s temple, fire descended from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and sacrifices, 98. This was a figure of the resurrection, in which all the righteous will be inflamed by divine love, ibid. The burial of a saint, in the sense of the Church, is his release from the bonds of the body, 78. To love God with all our heart, with all our soul, and with all our strength, and to love our neighbor as ourselves, is the Lord’s commandment, 97. Whoever hates his neighbor does not love God, 20. Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, ibid. Once God considered destroying the human being because of sins, 125. He who ought to have destroyed us because of transgression of the commandment promised, because of his mercy, that he would be our restorer, 130. God loves those whom he rebukes and chastises, 118. God is to be sought in goodness and simplicity, 94. A didrachm is a coin containing two drachmas, with which the tax was paid to Caesar, 100. We must not distrust the Lord’s compassion; rather, repentance for sins must be hastened, 19. Saint Dionysius, bishop of Milan, was tested by the heretics through deceit, 68.

## E
### E

The Church gathered from the ends of the earth, 64. What are the two kinds of almsgiving? 88. How great their merit is before God is demonstrated, 86, 88. Elizabeth, conscious of her old age, is ashamed that she is going to give birth; therefore she concealed herself for five months, 42. *Encaenia* was the name given to the solemnities of the consecration and dedication of a temple, 80, 93 ff. The bishop of the Church of Laodicea is rebuked by the Lord because he is naked, poor, and blind; these things are to be understood of inward defects, 124. In the Church’s earliest times the Eucharist was received by men with their palms joined together, but by women in shining linen cloths, 62 [Col. 0981]. Eve is a figure of the Church; for just as Eve was fashioned from Adam’s side, so the Church grew from Christ’s body and wound, 63. The truth of the Gospel is so certain that, even if an angel preached contrary to it, he should not be heard, 142. Collectors of the tribute, fearing Christ because of the multitude of miracles, ask Peter whether his Master paid the didrachma, 99. Saint Exuperantius, a disciple of Saint Eusebius of Vercelli and afterward bishop of Tortona, is commended, 67.

### F

The happiness of this world, when sought too eagerly, generally ends in sorrow and adversity, 115. That is the true and supreme festivity by which a person has died to vices and lives only for righteousness, 78. Christian faith, strengthened by the firmest testimonies, allows no disputation concerning its truth, 48.

### G

The angel Gabriel does not rebuke unbelief in Mary, as he does in Zechariah, but instructs her concerning the newness of the divine operation, 130. How great will the joy of God in heaven be? 78. Christ’s generation is ineffable and must be apprehended by faith, 46. Mary obtained the dignity of Mother of God and did not lose her virginal chastity, ibid.

### H

What did the heretics attempt to add to the Creed? 31. With what religious observance did the Hebrews keep the Sabbath day? 89. The heavenly punishment and most dreadful death of King Herod, the slayer of innocent children, are described, 27. The threefold dedication of the Jerusalem temple is recalled. The first was carried out by Solomon, the second by Zerubbabel and the priest Jeshua, and the third by Judas Maccabaeus. This is mentioned in the Gospel of John, chapter X, 96. *Holocaustum* is Greek; in Latin it is called *totum incensum* (“wholly burned”), 97. In Scripture, people are designated according to their vices by various names drawn from beasts, 125. The hour which Christ said at the feast in Cana of Galilee had not yet come, when speaking to his mother, is to be understood as the hour of his Passion, 103. The six water jars placed at the aforementioned feast are said to signify the six ages of the world, and their interpretation is given, 104 ff.

### I

Entrance into this world is alike for all, and departure is likewise alike, 24. Isaiah’s prophecy, “Behold, a virgin shall conceive,” etc., chapter VII, concerning the Lord’s coming, is so clear that the Jews who did not believe it are without excuse, 141.

### J

Jesus Christ, the Only-Begotten of God the Father, is in no respect unlike his Begetter in nature, inferior in power, or later in time, 95. He went to Jerusalem for the feast of the Dedication of the temple and walked in Solomon’s portico, 93. John the Baptist was sent before Christ to announce his coming, 25. Entreaty rather than pleasure brought him into being, 41. What mystery is contained in the fact that the days begin to diminish at John’s Nativity, but increase at Christ’s Nativity? 26. His praises are found in the Holy Scriptures, with God as their author, 37. Why is he given the name “angel”? 38. He is filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother’s womb, 39. His repentance in the desert, ibid. John the Baptist sent his disciples to Christ to ask him, “Who are you?” 101. They returned reporting the miracles Christ performed, by which he showed himself to be the true God, ibid. John arose for Christ and also died for Christ; while preaching the truth and rebuking Herod for incest, he was beheaded, 41. Some thought that John the Evangelist was the bridegroom whose wedding was celebrated at the feast in Cana of Galilee, and that, after seeing the miracle of water’s conversion into wine, he dismissed his bride and followed Christ, 106. The same John, reclining at the supper upon the Lord’s breast, drew in heavenly secrets, 142. Exiled to the island of Patmos, he wrote the divine book of the Apocalypse, 143. Job’s admirable fortitude amid the burden and squalor of every calamity is commended, 142. Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary, warned by an angel in a dream, departed from Egypt into the land of Israel with the child Jesus and his mother, 26. The Jews who refused to receive Jesus Christ will receive Antichrist, 90. They have always persecuted God’s prophets who foretold Christ’s coming, 91. Rash judgment concerning one’s neighbor is forbidden, 137.

### L

[Col. 0982] The Lacedaemonians trained boys by public beatings, so as to make them stronger for enduring the hardships of war, 117. The magnanimity of Lawrence is shown by the fact that, fearing not the emperor’s savagery, he distributed the Church’s treasures among the poor. His courage was admirable and singular when, placed upon the gridiron, he overcame the flames, 54 ff. Before Lawrence completed his martyrdom, he converted the pagan Hippolytus to the faith of Christ and joined him to himself as a companion in receiving the crown, 57. The poor Lazarus is received into Abraham’s bosom and rejoices, while the rich man burns in everlasting flames, 138. Luxury, when it attacks people with savage bite, holds them in chains, 118.

### M

The invincible Maccabean brothers endured the most atrocious torments to preserve the laws of their fathers, 70, 71, 75, etc. Their mother is celebrated for her admirable courage and steadfastness, 73, 76. Mary Magdalene, languishing with love at the tomb of Christ the Lord, deserved to find him, 30. The praises of Mary, Mother of God, are recounted, 43 ff. Her virginity before childbirth, in childbirth, and after childbirth is asserted and proved by the testimony of Scripture, 45, 47 ff. She alone among women gave birth to a son while her virginity remained intact, 131. The martyrs are crowned in heaven when their temporal struggle has ended, 95. Their commemorations are to be celebrated in the Church, 50. The kind of martyrdom by which Saint Eusebius of Vercelli was afflicted by the Arians is described, 70. The Church of Milan, made illustrious by the triumphs of many martyrs, 48. What holiness does the Eucharistic table require in those who approach it? 61. We have all been invited to it, but especially adorned with chastity and purity, 23. Mercy toward the poor repairs and sanctifies the evil use of riches, 23. In what places the sacrifice of the Mass is to be performed, 83. Monks instituted by Saint Eusebius of Vercelli to perform the duties of clerics in the Church. More concerning their institution and manner of life is found, 68 ff. Bodily death is not to be feared, but the death of the soul and eternal fire after death are, 55.

### N

With what purity of life one must approach the Lord’s Nativity, 17. Nazareth is interpreted as “flower,” or “shoot,” 28. The glorious passion of Saints Nazarius and Celsus is described, 47 ff.

### O

Hatred of one’s neighbor blinds the soul and turns it away from God, 20. Christ’s works bore witness to his divinity, 94. Servile works are not to be done on Sunday, that is, on the day commemorating the Lord’s Resurrection, 89. Prayer adorned with the merits of virtues is very effective with God, 50. But prayer made on behalf of those whose precepts we possess is heard, 87.

### P

The Paraclete Spirit strengthened the apostles in faith and heaped heavenly lights upon them, 35 ff. Parents are to be honored, and, if they are in need, assistance is to be given according to one’s means, 87. The patriarchs of the Old Testament could not be saved without hope in the future Redeemer, 129. The heretics called Patripassians denied the visibility and passibility of Christ’s flesh, 31. Saint Paul the apostle, caught up to the third heaven, learned to pour out his life for Christ, 134. A thorn of the flesh was given to him, so that through his struggle with it he might be perfected, 116. Past sins are to be redeemed through almsgiving and repentance, 23. Perseverance in virtue wins eternal salvation, 20. The heavenly kingdom is given to those who persevere to the end, 118. The distinction of the divine Persons is proved from that passage in John, chapter XIV: “And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete,” 31. Peter’s confession concerning Christ’s divinity, 96. His calling to catch human beings, 125. Peter entered the tomb and found the grave-cloths of the dead Christ, but did not find his body; therefore he announced that he had risen again, 30. Philip, called by Christ as an apostle, immediately brought Nathanael, a good and simple man, to him, 49. The heresy of Photinus is detestable: he blasphemously asserted that Christ was the same as the Father, 96. [Col. 0983] The prodigies formerly occurring at church dedications are recalled, 81. Everything that happened in the succession of time was foretold, 141. The first fruits of the earth’s harvest are to be offered to God, 85. **Promise.** The first promise of the future Restorer was made in the woman, by whom the serpent’s head was to be trodden underfoot, 130. The ancient prophets foretold everything up to Christ. After his coming, the apostles prophesied everything that remained, 141. Prudence must be joined to justice by those who preside over the ministry of the Church, 78. According to the Lord’s command, Christian prudence must not be separated from innocence, ibid.

### R

Ramah, which Jeremiah and Matthew mention, is not the name of a city or of any particular place, but means “on high,” 108. The relics of the holy martyrs are to be held in honor and veneration, 79 ff. The resurrection of the dead is established, 134. “When Christ, our life, appears, then we too shall appear with him in glory,” 55. The rites used in consecrating churches are explained, 79 ff.

### S

The queen of Sheba, from Ethiopia, came to King Solomon with a great retinue and precious gifts, etc.; the mystery of her coming is explained, 31. The heretics called Sabellians denied the real distinction of the divine Persons, 31. King Solomon, seduced and corrupted by women, turned the worship of the true God toward idols, 21. Certain of his difficult passages are explained intellectually, 58. When the saints rise again, they will possess their original integrity and the fullness of glory, 135. We are strengthened in this hope because in Christ we recognize the truth of his humanity, 136. Saul, transformed from a persecutor into a preacher of Christ and apostle to the Gentiles, 92. Nothing is to be taken away from the Holy Scriptures, 32. The Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, descended upon the apostles according to Christ’s promise, demonstrating that he had ascended into heaven and that he was the true God, 33. Saint Stephen, dying, besought God not to exact punishment from his persecutors but to grant them pardon, 144. Why white robes were given to the holy martyrs, as is read in the Apocalypse, 144. What does the word “Creed” signify? 29. It was composed by the apostles, who assembled together, 31. It is called a brief summary of faith because it contains the substance of the principal dogmas, ibid.

### T

What does the talent signify in the Gospel? 75 ff. With what magnificence Christians of ancient times cared for the adornment of temples, 84. [Col. 0984] The temple first built at Jerusalem by Solomon over seven years signifies the structure of the holy Church. This structure will continually increase for seven days, that is, for seven thousand years. And just as Solomon celebrated its dedication in the eighth year, so in the eighth thousand years the desired festivity of the righteous will occur, namely, the assumption of all into glory, 47. After its destruction, the same temple was rebuilt a second time in forty-six years—the number of days during which, according to some authorities, the human body is formed from conception in the differentiation of its members. Thus it was a figure of Christ’s body, the temple of the Holy Spirit, ibid. The apostle Thomas was confirmed in faith in Christ’s resurrection by touching his wounds, 36. **Tribe.** Christ was to be born according to the flesh from the tribe and lineage of David, 19 ff.

### V

There are many prophecies in Scripture concerning the Lord Christ’s birth from the lineage of David, 19 ff. How the prophecy of Psalm XXXIX concerning Christ is to be understood: “In the beginning of the book it is written of me,” 133. Likewise, the passage in Psalm XXII: “Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me,” ibid. The eternity of the divine Word and his undivided unity with the Father are asserted, 69. The way leading to the Lord is through straits and tribulations, not through pleasures, 113. For those who have sufficient food and clothing, everything else is superfluous; therefore it is to be distributed for the relief of the poor, 88. Saint Vincent the deacon was the firmer in confessing Christ the Lord the more bitter the torments by which he was tortured. Many prodigies made his martyrdom illustrious, 51 ff. Men assigned to sacred ministries attain perfection of life more easily when separated from association with the world, 39. The adornment of virtues, more splendid than gold and silver, is to be acquired so that we may worthily meet the Lord’s coming and deserve to receive him within ourselves, 17 ff., 22, 23, etc. **Vision of God.** In it prophecy and knowledge will cease, for everything will be naked and open, 142. Our life is exposed to daily calamities, 113. We shall be victorious over them if we bear them patiently, ibid. True life consists in knowing God, fearing his power, loving his goodness, and admiring the world in its Maker, 126. Anyone who wishes to have life must change his life, 17. How great is the obligation of the calling to Christ? 51.

### Z

When Zechariah was already advanced in age, an angel promised that a son would be born to Elizabeth, likewise an old and barren woman, 41, 96. **Belt.** What is to be understood by the leather belt with which John the Baptist was girded? 40. Zerubbabel, born of royal blood, and Jeshua the priest were responsible for the second dedication of the Jerusalem temple, in the spring, 96.

[Col. 0983]

## ORDER OF THE CONTENTS OF THIS VOLUME

[Col. 0983] Dedication letter, 9. Preface, 15. Life of Saint Maximus of Turin, 127. Testimonies concerning Saint Maximus. Schoenemann’s literary account of Saint Maximus of Turin, 177. Specimen of the manuscripts from which most of Saint Maximus’s works were extracted, 215.
